The other mutants involve missense mutations, in-frame insertions, or in-frame deletions that may alter the protein but are less likely to completely abolish its function.

Break: ATG TTT TAC GCT GGT GTC ACT TCT GTG... = 8 codons = 24 nucleotides. So there is an insertion of 3 nucleotides (one codon) and some substitutions. This is an in-frame insertion of one amino acid (Val) and some missense changes. It might not eliminate the compound, just alter it.

So there is a deletion of 3 nucleotides (one codon) and a substitution. This is an in-frame deletion of one amino acid (Gly) and a substitution. It might not eliminate the compound, just alter it.

Therefore, the mutation that will most probably eliminate the anti-nutritional compound is Mutant 2, which introduces a premature stop codon (TAA) early in the coding sequence. This will result in a truncated, non-functional protein.
